description: Figure 9 is a composite of three vertically stacked scatter plots, each plotting a nano-indentation elastic modulus against position. All three panels share the y-axis label "Elastic modulus Er [GPa]" with printed gridlines at 50, 150, 250, 350 and 450 GPa, and the common x-axis label "Position [μm]" with ticks at 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12 μm; dashed horizontal and vertical gridlines cross every panel. Data appear as blue filled diamond markers, about a dozen per panel, and no numeric data labels are printed on any point. In each panel a solid black upward arrow labelled "Grain boundary" marks the boundary on the x-axis — between the 3 and 6 μm gridlines close to the 6 line in the top and middle panels, and just right of the 6 μm line in the bottom panel. In all three panels the modulus is lowest at the marker immediately next to the grain boundary and higher away from it, the remaining markers scattering mostly between the 150 and 400 GPa gridlines. The three panels sit at different overall levels, which the citing text attributes to the differently oriented grains sampled. The figure therefore demonstrates a local reduction of elastic modulus at the grain boundary of each measurement line.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of elastic modulus vs position for one measurement line; blue diamond markers around the 150-300 GPa gridlines with a minimum at the marker just left of the upward 'Grain boundary' arrow (between the 3 and 6 μm gridlines) and values rising to about the 300 GPa gridline away from it.

Second scatter plot of elastic modulus vs position; markers dip to near the 150 GPa gridline at the 'Grain boundary' arrow (between the 3 and 6 μm gridlines) and increase toward the right, with the highest marker just below the 400 GPa gridline.

Third scatter plot of elastic modulus vs position; the 'Grain boundary' arrow sits just right of the 6 μm gridline, where a single marker lies near the 50 GPa gridline, with values rising to about the 250-280 GPa gridlines toward 12 μm.

observations.observation: The figure is three vertically stacked scatter plots sharing the y-axis label 'Elastic modulus Er [GPa]' with gridline labels 50, 150, 250, 350 and 450, and the x-axis label 'Position [μm]' with ticks at 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12 μm.
All data points are plotted as blue filled diamonds and no numeric values are printed next to the points; values can only be read relative to the dashed gridlines.
Every panel contains a solid black upward arrow annotated 'Grain boundary' marking the grain-boundary position on the x-axis.
In each of the three panels the lowest elastic modulus marker lies immediately adjacent to the grain-boundary arrow, showing a local modulus minimum at the boundary.
The grain-boundary arrow is located between the 3 and 6 μm gridlines, close to the 6 μm line, in the top and middle panels, and just right of the 6 μm line in the bottom panel.
Away from the grain boundary the markers scatter roughly between the 150 and 400 GPa gridlines, and the three panels sit at clearly different overall levels.
The caption states the figure presents the resulting Young's modulus for nano-indentation.
The citing text states nano-indentation with a spherical tip was used to measure the mechanical properties near a grain of the specimens.
The citing text states Fig. 8 shows one of the load-displacement curves with a nominal radius of R = 50 μm, from which the elastic properties of Fig. 9 were derived.

The citing text states the elastic modulus near the boundary has a smaller value than in the other regions, which have a similar distribution of values but at a different level because the grains are at different orientations.
The citing text states the measurement points lie along one of three lines across the boundary, consistent with the three stacked plots representing three separate measurement lines.
